academia_subtitulo: Short lessons: I tell you, I show you, and then you do it yourself in the park.
academia_demo_en_curso: Watch: I'm driving now. When I'm done, it's your turn.
academia_tutor_conduce: The tutor has the camera: Watch
academia_practica_intro: Your turn. Complete the tasks. If you get stuck, I'll whisper you a hint.
academia_practica_superada: Practice passed! Keep playing with it or go back to the menu.
academia_exposicion_superada: Tip: Turn on third stops in Options for finer control in the game. Each move will shift a third; with {paso_entero}, a full stop.
academia_foto_demo: Here's how the photo comes out
academia_teclas: Enter: Next · Backspace: Back · P: Pause the scene

esquema_estrellas_no: The streetlight is a round blob
esquema_corredor: Runner at %.1f m/s, %.0f m away · 1/%d s
esquema_congelado: Frozen if it stays under ~0.1 mm · Handheld: 1/%d or faster
esquema_arbol: %.0f mm · the tree looks %.1f times the person's height

esquema_angular: Wide angle up close: Background small and far
esquema_tercios_aire: Right crossing, but no room ahead
academia_ex_cuerpo_mal: This exam is with the TLR: Pick it on the panel.
academia_ex_sin_persona: There's nobody under the focus point.
academia_ex_iso_mal: ISO %d: The exam asks for ISO 100. Open the aperture more instead of raising it.
academia_ex_lado_ok: The person is to one side of the frame.
academia_ex_lado_mal: The person is in the center or out of the photo: Put them to one side.
academia_ex_sujeto_ok: The person is inside the sharp zone.
academia_ex_sujeto_mal: The person isn't sharp: Focus ended up at another distance.
academia_ex_medicion_mal: The exam asks for spot metering: Pick it on the panel.
academia_ex_modo_mal: This exam is in M: Pick it on the panel.
academia_ex_manual_mal: This exam is with manual focus.
academia_ex_focal_mal: You're at %d mm: The exam asks for the zoom at 70 mm or more.
academia_ex_comp_ok: Compensated to %s EV: Brighter, as asked.
academia_ex_comp_mal: Compensation at %s EV: The exam asks for +1 EV or more.
academia_ex_abierto_mal: At f/%s the background doesn't blur enough: Open up to f/2.8 or wider.
academia_ex_angular_mal: You're at %d mm: The exam asks for 24 mm.
academia_examen_intro: No hints. Shoot when you've got it and I'll tell you what went well and what didn't.
academia_examen_intentos: Attempts: %d. You can retake it as many times as you like.
academia_examen_superado: Exam passed. You can retake it to improve your score.
academia_ex_expo_mal: Exposure: You're off by %s EV. Move the aperture or the shutter speed until the dot lights up.
academia_ex_pulso_ok: Steady hands: 1/%d s with a %d mm.
academia_ex_pulso_mal: Camera shake: At 1/%d s with a %d mm your hands show. Use 1/%d s or faster.
academia_ex_dos_ok: Both people fit in the sharp zone (from %s to %s m).
academia_ex_dos_mal: The sharp zone goes from %s to %s m and they're at %s and %s m. Stop down or focus between the two.
academia_ex_dos_fuera: Both of them have to be in the photo.
academia_ex_corredor_mal: That person isn't running: The exam is with the runner.
academia_ex_congelado_mal: The runner is blurred at 1/%d s: You need 1/%d s or faster.
academia_ex_tercios_listo: The head is on a thirds crossing, with room ahead.
academia_ex_tercios_cruce: The head isn't on any thirds crossing.
academia_ex_tercios_aire: The head is on a crossing, but the room is behind them: Leave it in front.
academia_ex_tele_ok: %d mm telephoto: The background gets compressed.
academia_ex_tele_mal: You shot at %d mm: The exam asks for the 135 mm telephoto.
academia_ex_lejos_ok: Full body from %s m: The background stays glued to their back.
academia_ex_lejos_mal: The person fills %d %% of the height, at %s m. Find someone far away (over 9 m) filling between 45 and 130 %%.
academia_ex_nitido_mal: Subject out of focus (%.3f mm; sharp goes up to 0.030 mm).
academia_composicion_resumen: Where to put things so the photo can breathe.
academia_composicion_t1_texto: Every lesson has four parts. First, the theory: Read each page and press “Next”. Then a demo where the camera drives itself. Then comes the practice, and you'll be told when you're in charge. Finally, an exam.
academia_composicion_t2_texto: Split the viewfinder in three with two vertical lines and two horizontal ones. Whatever sits on them, or where they cross, almost always works better than dead center: The eye has room to wander. In practice, show them with {tercios}.
academia_composicion_t3_texto: If someone is walking or looking to one side, leave them space in front: That's where the story happens. Stuck to the edge they're heading for, they'll look like they're about to walk into the frame.
academia_composicion_t4_texto: In a portrait, the face looks great near the top third. And a classic: Never crop anyone at a joint (knees, ankles). Better a little before or a little after.
academia_composicion_t5_texto: So is centering forbidden? Not at all: With symmetry, or when you want something bold, it's perfect. But master the thirds first: It's the shortest road to photos that breathe.
academia_composicion_d1: I bring up the thirds grid ({tercios}).
academia_composicion_d2: This person is walking. If I center them…
academia_composicion_d4: I move them to a third and leave room toward where they're going.
academia_composicion_d5: The face near the top line. Now we're talking! I shoot.
academia_composicion_p2: Put someone's head on a crossing of the lines
academia_composicion_p3: …with room toward where they're going, and shoot
academia_composicion_pista_cuadricula: Press {tercios} to see the thirds lines.
academia_composicion_pista_cruce: Frame someone and place their head on one of the four line crossings.
academia_composicion_pista_aire: Good crossing, but they're walking toward the near edge: Use the crossing on the other side.
academia_composicion_pista_listo: Head on the crossing and room ahead! Shoot with {disparar}.
academia_composicion_pista_foto_no: In that photo the head wasn't on a crossing with room ahead. Try again.
academia_composicion_examen: EXAM. Your model is walking along the path. Frame them with their head on a thirds crossing and with room ahead, toward where they're going.
academia_enfoque_t1_texto: The camera doesn't know who your star is. It focuses on whatever is under the focus point, be it a person or a streetlight. So half of focusing well is aiming well. The other half is coming up.
academia_enfoque_t2_texto: This camera doesn't have one focus point: It has nine. If your star is off to one side, pick the point on that side ({punto_enfoque}) instead of re-centering them. The framing calls the shots. The point obeys.
academia_enfoque_t3_texto: The oldest trick in the book: Focus on someone in the center, lock it ({bloqueo}) and turn the camera to put them where you want. Focus stays at that distance even if the point is now aimed at something else.
academia_enfoque_t4_texto: And what if the camera insists on focusing on the fence in front? You take the wheel. With manual focus we decide the distance, and it stays put. Slow, sure. But nobody argues with us.
academia_enfoque_d1: I focus on this person with the center point. Beep: Done.
academia_enfoque_d2: I lock focus. It won't budge from that distance now.
academia_enfoque_d3: And now I turn the camera to put them to one side, with room.
academia_enfoque_d4: The point is aimed at the background, but they're still sharp. I shoot.
academia_enfoque_d5: Focus, lock, reframe. Three moves, a better photo.
academia_enfoque_p1: Pick a focus point other than the center one
academia_enfoque_p2: Focus on someone and lock focus
academia_enfoque_p3: Reframe to put them to one side, and shoot
academia_enfoque_pista_bloquea: Aim at someone and lock with {bloqueo}.
academia_enfoque_pista_reencuadra: Locked. Turn the camera until they're to one side and shoot with {disparar}.
academia_enfoque_pista_foto_no: In that photo they weren't both to one side and sharp. Lock and reframe again.
academia_enfoque_examen: EXAM. The camera is on manual focus and out of focus. Make the person near you sharp by turning the ring ({enfoque_mf}).
academia_focal_resumen: Why telephoto squashes and wide angle stretches.
academia_focal_t1_texto: The easy part: A wide angle (28 mm) takes in a lot and a telephoto (135 mm), very little. Now the fun part: What happens to the background when we swap one for the other. We've all seen it on a thousand movie posters.
academia_focal_t2_texto: With the 28 mm you have to get right up close for the person to fill the photo. And the background? Tiny and miles away. Everything looks farther apart than it is: Perspective gets exaggerated.
academia_focal_t3_texto: With the 135 mm you do the opposite: Step way back to get the same framing. And suddenly the background looks huge, glued to the person's back. The planes squash against each other.
academia_focal_t4_texto: The final twist: Focal length doesn't change perspective. WHERE we stand does. Focal length only decides how much is cropped. Telephoto “squashes” because it makes you step back; wide angle “stretches” because it makes you get close.
academia_focal_d1: With the 28 mm I frame someone close by, about 2 m away.
academia_focal_d2: I shoot: The background, small and far.
academia_focal_d3: I switch to the 135 mm and look for someone far off, by the trees.
academia_focal_d4: I shoot: The trees are huge and right behind them.
academia_focal_d5: Same person in the frame, opposite backgrounds. That's compression.
academia_focal_p1: With the 28 mm, a full-body photo of someone close (under 4.5 m)
academia_focal_p2: With the 135 mm, a full-body photo of someone over 9 m away
academia_focal_pista_angular: Put on the 28 mm (panel button) and frame someone on the bench path, full body.
academia_focal_pista_tele: Put on the 135 mm (panel button) and find someone far away: The outer path or the people on the meadow, at the back.
academia_focal_pista_lejos: That person is too close for the telephoto: Find someone over 9 m away, like the people on the meadow, at the back.
academia_focal_pista_cerca: With the wide angle, find someone close, under 4.5 m away (the bench path).
academia_focal_pista_tamano: Frame them full body: Have them fill almost the whole height of the photo.
academia_focal_examen: EXAM. Your model is far away. Take a full-body photo of them with the lens that makes the background look glued to their back.
academia_exposicion_resumen: Three taps for the same light, and the trick to mix them.
academia_exposicion_t1_titulo: A photo is a bucket of light
academia_exposicion_t1_texto: A photo is a bucket of light: Dark if it isn't full, blown out if it overflows. You fill it with aperture, shutter speed and sensitivity. The meter (+ ● −) guides you: The dot lights up when it's right; + and − mean too much or too little.
academia_exposicion_t2_texto: It's the hole the light comes through. The number runs backwards: Small number (f/2), BIG hole. Big number (f/16), small hole. Each stop (f/2.8 → f/4 → f/5.6…) lets in exactly half the light. Change it with {diafragma_y}.
academia_exposicion_t3_texto: It's how long the tap stays open. At 1/60 s twice as much light gets in as at 1/125 s. With too much time the photo comes out blurred, because the world won't stop and wait for us. Change it with {velocidad_y}.
academia_exposicion_t4_texto: With a faint recording, turning up the volume makes it louder, but noisier. Here it's measured in ISO: 200 needs half the light of 100, but adds noise. It's the wild card for when the other two can't give any more. Change it with {iso_y}.
academia_exposicion_t5_texto: The three taps speak the same language: Stops. One stop is double or half the light. Close the aperture one stop? Add one stop of time or sensitivity and nothing changes. That's the exposure triangle.
academia_exposicion_t6_texto: Sometimes we'll want the photo brighter or darker than the camera says. But, as with the rest of the course, first we'll learn to do it the right way. Then we'll break the rules.
academia_exposicion_d1: We start with the dot lit: The photo would come out well exposed.
academia_exposicion_d2: If I now stop down two stops, from f/4 to f/8…
academia_exposicion_d3: …the dot goes out and the − sign is left: We're two stops short on light.
academia_exposicion_d4: How do I fix it? Shutter speed two stops slower and…
academia_exposicion_d5: …the dot is back! Same light, another recipe.
academia_exposicion_d6: Once more: I raise the ISO two stops and now it's too much. The + lights up…
academia_exposicion_d7: …so I stop down the aperture two more. The dot, again.
academia_exposicion_d8: I shoot to check: Well exposed. Three recipes, the same photo.
academia_exposicion_p1: Stop down the aperture to f/11
academia_exposicion_p2: Compensate with the shutter speed until the dot lights up
academia_exposicion_pista_cerrar: Stop down the aperture ({diafragma}): It's at f/%s now.
academia_exposicion_pista_oscura: The light meter reads %s: Not enough light. Try a slower shutter speed ({velocidad}).
academia_exposicion_pista_clara: The light meter reads %s: Too much light. Try a faster shutter speed ({velocidad}).
academia_exposicion_pista_foto_mal: That photo was off by %s stops. Wait for the dot to light up before you shoot.
academia_exposicion_examen: EXAM. It has suddenly clouded over and your settings no longer work: The light meter reads about 3 EV short. Get the dot to light up again with the aperture, shutter speed or ISO, and shoot.
academia_dof_resumen: Why the background melts away, and how to get it.
academia_dof_t1_texto: Seen those portraits with a soft background? It isn't magic. A lens only truly focuses at ONE distance. A little in front and a little behind still look fine. That band is the depth of field. It's drawn in the diagram.
academia_dof_t2_texto: And who decides how wide that band is? The aperture. Wide open (f/1.8): A razor-thin band, and the background melts into soft blobs (the famous “bokeh”). Stopped down (f/11, f/16): The band grows and almost everything is sharp.
academia_dof_t3_texto: It has two accomplices: Focal length and distance. A telephoto at 4 m isolates a person as if the world around them had been cut away. A wide angle keeps almost everything sharp, even when you don't want it to.
academia_dof_t4_texto: Here's the catch: Only one plane is perfectly sharp. Everything else is dots that keep growing. As long as they measure under 0.03 mm on the negative, the eye buys it. That limit is the circle of confusion, and it's what sets the band.
academia_dof_t5_texto: At night the aperture pulls another trick. Wide open, each streetlight is a round blob. Stopped down (f/11, f/16), its blades turn it into a star, longer the more you close. It shows in the photo: The viewfinder looks wide open.
academia_dof_d1: I focus on this person, about 4 m away, with the 105 mm at f/1.8.
academia_dof_d2: Look at the diagram: The sharp band is a hand's width: That's tiny.
academia_dof_d3: And the background, pure cream: That's bokeh. I shoot.
academia_dof_d4: Now I stop down to f/11, one stop at a time. The camera compensates the speed…
academia_dof_d5: The band grows past a meter and the background comes back.
academia_dof_d6: I shoot at f/11. Compare: The same scene, two different backgrounds.
academia_dof_p1: Focus on someone between 3 and 6 m away
academia_dof_p2: Take a photo at f/2.8 or wider, with the background blurred
academia_dof_p3: Take another at f/8 or narrower and compare them
academia_dof_intro: Your turn. The camera sets the shutter speed for you: You only move the aperture.
academia_dof_pista_enfoca: Focus on a nearby person with {af} (now at %s).
academia_dof_pista_abre: Open the aperture ({diafragma}) to f/2.8 or less and shoot.
academia_dof_pista_cierra: Now stop down ({diafragma}) to f/8 or more and shoot.
academia_dof_examen: EXAM. Two people, one quite a bit farther away than the other, and a single photo where both come out sharp. You'll have to stop down a lot… and think hard about where to focus.
academia_movimiento_resumen: Freeze a runner… or let them fly.
academia_movimiento_t1_texto: While the shutter is open, the world goes about its business. With a long time, whatever moves leaves a trail, like a ghost. With a very short one (1/500, 1/1000), it's frozen in midair, with both feet off the ground.
academia_movimiento_t2_texto: It depends on who you're chasing. A walker freezes at 1/125, but a runner asks for 1/500 or more. And watch out: The closer you are and the longer the lens, the faster everything flies out of the photo.
academia_movimiento_t3_texto: Plot twist: Even if nobody moves, we do. The handheld rule: Never go below 1/focal length. At 50 mm, 1/60 s at least, and at 100 mm, 1/125. Below that, the photo shakes and it's our fault.
academia_movimiento_t4_texto: Nothing comes free: A very short time lets in very little light. You'll have to open the aperture or raise the ISO. Sound familiar? It's trading stops, from the exposure lesson. We told you it was good for everything.
academia_movimiento_t5_texto: Or the other way round: Follow the runner and shoot slow (1/30) as you turn. Runner sharp, background in streaks: That's panning. On the keyboard, hold the turn key toward where they run: The camera keeps pace and says so (“Tracking”).
academia_movimiento_d1: Here comes a runner. I set 1/30 s and the camera compensates the light…
academia_movimiento_d2: …I shoot and out comes a ghost. 1/30 isn't even close.
academia_movimiento_d3: I go up to 1/1000. The price: The camera has to open the aperture.
academia_movimiento_d4: I shoot again: Frozen in full flight.
academia_movimiento_d5: Remember: With a 50 mm, handheld, never below 1/60.
academia_movimiento_d6: And panning: Back to 1/30, and I hold the turn key toward where they run…
academia_movimiento_d7: …the camera keeps pace and I shoot, holding on: Runner sharp, background streaked.
academia_movimiento_p1: Photo of the runner at 1/60 or slower: Look at the trail
academia_movimiento_p2: Freeze them: Photo of the runner at 1/500 or faster
academia_movimiento_p3: Pan at 1/30: Follow them with the turn key
academia_movimiento_intro: Your turn. You set the shutter speed. The camera focuses on the runner and sets the light.
academia_movimiento_pista_espera: The runner goes by every few seconds. The camera focuses on its own: You shoot when they cross.
academia_movimiento_pista_lenta: Set a slow shutter speed ({velocidad}), 1/60 or less.
academia_movimiento_pista_rapida: Now raise the shutter speed ({velocidad}) to 1/500 or more and shoot when they cross.
academia_movimiento_pista_barrido: Set 1/30 and hold {girar} toward where they run: When you see “Tracking subject”, shoot without letting go.
academia_movimiento_pista_barrido_movido: It's blurred: Don't let go of the turn key until after you shoot.
academia_movimiento_pista_no_corredor: The runner wasn't in the photo: Wait for them to cross the frame.
academia_movimiento_examen: EXAM. Now with the zoom at 70 mm, where everything moves faster: I want the runner completely frozen, and no camera shake.
academia_medicion_resumen: What the light meter looks at before giving its opinion.
academia_medicion_t1_texto: You've been listening to the light meter since the exposure lesson. But what light is it measuring? It depends on what you ask it. It has three ways of looking, and the same scene can give you three different answers.
academia_medicion_t2_texto: Matrix looks at the whole scene and takes the average. With an even landscape it's perfect. With a person in the shade and the background in the sun, it isn't: The background wins by majority and the star of the photo comes out dark.
academia_medicion_t3_texto: It looks at everything, but gives the center more weight, since that's usually where the important stuff is. The good old middle ground: It fails less than matrix with backlight, and it doesn't ask for as much aim as the next one.
academia_medicion_t4_texto: It measures only what's under the focus point and ignores the rest. It's a scalpel: Aim at your star and it comes out right, whatever's behind. But aim badly and it makes a mess. Too dark or too bright? That's what compensation is for.
academia_medicion_t5_texto: The camera always tries to make the scene a middle tone. At night that's a lie: It brightens what should look dark. For a night photo to look natural, compensate to −1 or −2 EV, like now. We're the boss, not the light meter.
academia_medicion_d1: With matrix metering, the camera averages the whole scene.
academia_medicion_d2: I switch to center-weighted: Now the center rules. See how the exposure changes?
academia_medicion_d3: And spot: Only what's under the point counts. This person.
academia_medicion_d4: If I still want them brighter, I compensate: +1 EV.
academia_medicion_d5: I put it back and shoot: Exposed for them.
academia_medicion_p2: Raise the compensation to +1 EV and watch it change
academia_medicion_p3: Go back to 0 and take a well-exposed photo
academia_medicion_pista_puntual: Pick “Spot” on the panel: It'll meter only under the focus point.
academia_medicion_pista_compensa: Raise the compensation to +1 EV: Pick it with {elegir_control} and change it with {cambiar_control}.
academia_medicion_pista_cero: Bring it back to 0 and shoot, aiming at a person.
academia_medicion_pista_foto_no: That photo wasn't well exposed with the compensation at 0. Again.
academia_medicion_examen: EXAM. I want a bright portrait: Meter on the person with spot metering and make it one stop brighter than the camera says.
academia_modos_resumen: Who decides what: You, the camera or both.
academia_modos_t1_texto: Aperture, shutter speed, ISO: Someone has to decide them. The modes are how that work is split between us and the camera. Four letters that have been on cameras for half a century. Let's go from least to most control.
academia_modos_t2_texto: In P (program) the camera picks aperture and shutter speed, and our only job is to compensate the exposure if needed. It nearly always gets the light right. What it can't know is the photo we want: A blurred background or a frozen runner.
academia_modos_t3_texto: In A we pick the aperture and the camera sets the shutter speed: What you did in depth of field. It's the mode for thinking about the background: Wide open to blur it, stopped down for everything sharp. Watch how the speed changes.
academia_modos_t4_texto: S is the other way round: We set the shutter speed and the camera the aperture, like with the runner. The mode for thinking about motion: 1/1000 to freeze, 1/30 for a pan. If there isn't enough light, the light meter tells on it.
academia_modos_t5_texto: In M the camera decides nothing: We set both and the light meter just gives its opinion. Why bother? Because then the exposure doesn't change from one photo to the next, even if the framing does. It's what you did in the exposure lesson.
academia_modos_d1: In P the camera sets everything. I just frame.
academia_modos_d2: I switch to A and open the aperture: The shutter speed adjusts itself.
academia_modos_d3: I switch to S and raise the speed: Now it's the aperture that moves.
academia_modos_d4: And in M nothing moves unless I move it.
academia_modos_d5: I light the dot by hand and shoot. Same result, another road.
academia_modos_p1: In A: A photo at f/4 or wider
academia_modos_p2: In S: A photo at 1/500 or faster
academia_modos_p3: In M: A well-exposed photo (with the dot lit)
academia_modos_pista_p: You're in P: Pick A, S or M on the panel.
academia_modos_pista_a: Pick A on the panel, open the aperture ({diafragma}) to f/4 or less and shoot.
academia_modos_pista_s: Pick S, raise the shutter speed ({velocidad}) to 1/500 or more and shoot.
academia_modos_pista_m: Pick M and center the light meter yourself: Right now it reads %s.
academia_modos_pista_foto_no: In M that photo was off by %s stops. Center the light meter before you shoot.
academia_modos_examen: EXAM. I want the person sharp and the background blurred: At f/2.8 or wider, and well exposed. You choose the mode.
academia_objetivos_resumen: Zoom or prime: Convenience versus light.
academia_objetivos_t1_titulo: Focal length: How much you see
academia_objetivos_t1_texto: The lens number (24, 50, 105 mm) says how much world fits: Small, a lot. Big, a little and up close. Right now there's a 24 on: Half the park fits. A 50 sees roughly like we do. So far, so easy.
academia_objetivos_t2_texto: A zoom is lots of focal lengths in one tube. This one is a “24–105 f/4”: From 24 to 105 mm, and f/4 is its biggest hole. Others have two apertures, like “24–120 f/2.8–5.6”: At 24 mm it opens up to f/2.8, but at 120 mm only to f/5.6.
academia_objetivos_t3_texto: A prime has a single focal length. Who'd want that? Its name says it: “50 mm f/1.8”. Over two stops above the zoom: Five times more light gets in. That's where the speed it asks for now comes from, with the same light as before.
academia_objetivos_t4_texto: That's why a lens that opens wide is called “fast”: In low light it lets you shoot handheld where the zoom forces camera shake or a higher ISO. And the zoom? You do it with your feet. No joke.
academia_objetivos_d1: Blue hour, low light. The 24–105 zoom at f/4 and ISO 100 wants a very slow speed…
academia_objetivos_d2: …I shoot handheld and it comes out shaky. No miracles here.
academia_objetivos_d3: I switch to the 50 mm prime and open it to f/1.8: Over two stops for free.
academia_objetivos_d4: Now the speed is fast enough to hold. I shoot: Sharp.
academia_objetivos_d5: Same light, same ISO. The difference was the hole.
academia_objetivos_p1: With the zoom at f/4 and ISO 100, center the meter and check the speed
academia_objetivos_p2: With the prime at f/1.8 and ISO 100, center it again
academia_objetivos_p3: Shoot with the prime: No shake and well exposed
academia_objetivos_pista_zoom: Zoom at f/4 and ISO 100: Lower the shutter speed ({velocidad}) until it centers. You're at 1/%d s.
academia_objetivos_pista_fijo: Switch to the prime (panel), open it to f/1.8 ({diafragma}) and center again with the shutter speed.
academia_objetivos_pista_dispara: You're at 1/%d s: With a 50 mm your hands hold from 1/60. Shoot.
academia_objetivos_pista_trepidada: Shaky: 1/%d s is too slow for a 50 mm handheld.
academia_objetivos_examen: EXAM. Blue hour. I need a wide shot at 24 mm, handheld and well exposed. Only one of your two lenses goes down to 24.
academia_camaras_resumen: Four ways of looking at the same park.
academia_camaras_t1_texto: Every camera does the same thing: Let light in for a while. What changes, a lot, is how you look through it. And that changes how you shoot. Let's go through the game's four, starting with the one on screen now.
academia_camaras_t2_texto: It does everything itself: Focuses, exposes and shows you the photo on a little screen. It's the “point and shoot” camera. The bad part? It decides for us. The good part? We never miss the shot while we're thinking.
academia_camaras_t3_texto: Decades ago it was the standard: You look through a little window beside the lens, not through it, and focus by hand until the double image in the center merges. The view never changes: Frame lines show what the photo will take.
academia_camaras_t4_texto: A mirror shows exactly what the lens sees. What you see is what you get: The zoom, the blur, everything. That's why it gets on so well with huge telephotos. The mirror flips up when you shoot: Hence the viewfinder blink.
academia_camaras_t5_texto: 80 years ago people shot with two lenses: One for the photo and one for looking. You hold it at your waist, and the mirror flips the image: Turn left and everything slides right. Those are the square photos Instagram brought back.
academia_camaras_t6_texto: Today the most common are the phone, which decides almost everything on its own, and mirrorless cameras with interchangeable lenses, which show on a screen what the sensor sees. In this game, for now, we don't use them.
academia_camaras_d1: The compact: Screen, zoom and everything automatic.
academia_camaras_d2: The rangefinder: A window with its frame. The double image in the center is the focus.
academia_camaras_d3: The SLR: I see exactly what the lens sees, with its red lights underneath.
academia_camaras_d4: The TLR: I look down into it, square and flipped. I turn one way… it goes the other.
academia_camaras_d5: And I shoot with it. Twelve shots per roll: Here you think first.
academia_camaras_p1: A sharp photo of a person with the rangefinder
academia_camaras_p2: Another with the TLR (careful, it's flipped!)
academia_camaras_pista_telemetrica: Pick the rangefinder on the panel and merge the double image on someone with {enfoque_mf}.
academia_camaras_pista_tlr: Now the TLR: Focus with {enfoque_mf} and remember the viewfinder is flipped (the photo comes out right).
academia_camaras_pista_reflex: And the SLR: Aim at someone, focus with {af} and shoot.
academia_camaras_pista_borrosa: That one wasn't sharp, or there was nobody under the focus point. Again.
academia_camaras_examen: EXAM. You look down into the TLR and it's flipped. Take a sharp photo of a person with it.
arcade_subtitulo: Thirty levels. Each one sets the setting, the light and the camera, and asks for something different. Clear one to unlock the next.
arcade_aviso_nubes: Watch out for clouds: They darken the area as they pass.
arcade_aviso_tercios: Tip: Turn on third stops in Options for finer control.
arcade_aviso_tercios_nivel: In this level the dials move in third stops.
arcade_aviso_barrido: Hold the turn key toward where they run and shoot without letting go.

cond_congelado_lento: at %d mm you need 1/%d s or faster. You used 1/%d s

cond_barrido_corto: the background barely streaks (%.1f mm at 1/%d s): Use a slower speed, like 1/30 s
cond_barrido_corto_focal: the background barely streaks (%.1f mm at 1/%d s): Zoom in or wait for them to pass closer
cond_focal_max: Focal length · at most %.0f mm (%.0f mm)
cond_aire_ok: there's room toward where they're walking
cond_aire_falta: the room is behind them: Leave it on the side they're walking toward
cond_aire_quieto: they're not crossing the frame: Wait until they walk sideways
cond_exposicion: Spot-on exposure · %+.2f EV from the meter's zero (up to ±0.25)
cond_nitido: Everything sharp · blur 10 m behind %.3f mm (sharp up to 0.030)
cond_actividad_no: they're not doing anything right now: Wait until they sit down
cond_corta_actividad: While they read, check their phone, drink coffee or feed the birds
cond_perro_fuera: the dog isn't in the frame
cond_perro_borroso: the dog is out of focus (%.3f mm): Stop down
cond_luz_no: the sun isn't behind them: Face the sun, with your subject in between
cond_luz_sombra: your subject is in the shade: Wait for the sun to reach them
cond_luz_oscura: the face is too dark: Meter on it and compensate toward +2
cond_silueta_negra: too dark: The sky goes dark too
cond_silueta_clara: you can make out their clothes: Expose one to two stops under
cond_corta_contraluz: Backlit, with the face well exposed
cond_estela_ok: at 1/%d s the runner leaves a %.1f mm trail
cond_estela_camara: the background is blurred: Don't turn the camera while you shoot
cond_estela_corta: they barely move (%.1f mm at 1/%d s): Use a slower speed
cond_corta_estela: Runner as a trail, sharp background
cond_corta_estrella: Lights as stars: f/11 or narrower
cond_estrella_ok: f/%s with %d lights in the frame
cond_estrella_abierto: at f/%s the lights don't make stars: Stop down to f/11 or more
cond_estrella_sin_luz: there's no light in the frame: Include a streetlight or the bandstand
cond_pulso_lento: at 1/%d s the photo shakes: Don't go below 1/%d s
cond_quieto_movido: the person is blurred at 1/%d s: Find someone who's standing still
arcade_cualquiera: Anyone you like, as long as they're still
arcade_nadie: There's nobody in the photo: Frame a person.
arcade_nivel_1_texto: Find the person and take their photo. The compact does everything.
arcade_nivel_2_texto: They must fill at least 60 % of the photo's height: Use the zoom.
arcade_nivel_3_texto: Nobody else must show up in the frame.
arcade_nivel_4_texto: Exactly one more person in the frame, within 90 seconds: Wait for them to cross paths.
arcade_nivel_5_texto: Put their face on a golden line, not in the center.
arcade_nivel_6_texto: Shoot at 135 mm or more. With that much zoom they won't fit whole: Frame the face.
arcade_nivel_7_texto: Wide angle, at 35 mm or less, and leave room on the side they're walking toward: A photo breathes where its subject is heading.
arcade_nivel_8_texto: Aperture priority: You pick the aperture ({diafragma}) and the camera does the rest. Open it up to blur the background.
arcade_nivel_9_texto: They say you should focus on the eyes. Our mannequins don't have any, so we'll settle for the face: Put the single-point AF right on it.
arcade_nivel_10_texto: Shutter priority: You pick the time ({velocidad}) and the camera does the rest. A runner with a telephoto needs 1/2000 s or faster; the more zoom, the faster.
arcade_nivel_11_texto: The rangefinder has no autofocus: Overlap the double image (wheel or R/T). Exposure is still automatic and people walk slower.
arcade_nivel_12_texto: Find your subject while you stroll, with nobody else in the photo.
arcade_nivel_13_texto: Your subject sits on a bench to read, check their phone, drink coffee or feed the birds. Photograph them while they do it, with a sharp face (still no eyes).
arcade_nivel_14_texto: Your subject and the bandstand in one photo, both sharp: Stop down ({diafragma}) and wait for them to walk past it.
arcade_nivel_15_texto: All manual for the first time: The exposure starts out well metered. Adjust it with the light meter. And get close: The subject must fill at least half the photo.
arcade_nivel_16_texto: Low light: Aperture priority. Wide-open aperture and manual focus on the face, which is where the eyes would be.
arcade_nivel_17_texto: All manual, with clouds: Leave the light meter at zero, off by a quarter stop at most. Here the dials move in thirds: With full stops it would be down to luck.
arcade_nivel_18_texto: The sun behind your subject: The camera meters that sun and leaves the face dark. Face the sun, spot-meter on your subject and compensate toward +2 ({compensacion}).
arcade_nivel_19_texto: Same sun, opposite intent: Your subject in black against the sky. Facing the sun, expose one to two stops below what the light meter asks for.
arcade_nivel_20_texto: Stop down to f/11 or more and the lights become stars. Get 1/30 s or faster: You'll have to play with the setting you can spare. That's slower than a 50 mm can hold: Hold your breath and find someone still.
arcade_nivel_21_texto: You look down into the TLR and the viewfinder swaps left and right. Everything is manual, no rush.
arcade_nivel_22_texto: Golden ratio in the square, with the image flipped.
arcade_nivel_23_texto: Portrait at sunset: Sharp face (the loupe will show you there are no eyes), blurred background and a big subject. Open the aperture and compensate with the shutter speed.
arcade_nivel_24_texto: Freeze a runner with the TLR: You need 1/1000 s, its fastest speed.
arcade_nivel_25_texto: A single shot, 60 seconds, a sharp face and nobody else.
arcade_nivel_26_texto: The pan: Set 1/30 s, hold {girar} toward where they run and wait. The camera matches their pace (“Tracking subject”): Shoot without letting go. Runner sharp, background streaked. With mouse or pad, it's all your hand.
arcade_nivel_27_texto: The opposite of panning: Camera still and a slow speed, from 1/30 s to 1/8 s (at this hour they won't burn the photo). Let go of the turn keys: The park comes out sharp and the runner, a trail.
arcade_nivel_28_texto: With the 105 mm: Blurred background and the person on the golden ratio.
arcade_nivel_29_texto: Find whoever's walking the dog: Both in the frame and both sharp, all manual. The owner must fill at least 40 % of the height.
arcade_nivel_30_texto: Two shots, at night and all manual: Put the focus point on the face. Make it big, with nobody else.

ayuda_texto_teclado:
Look: Drag with the mouse (the view goes where you move it) or ⟦←⟧⟦→⟧⟦↑⟧⟦↓⟧ · ⟦A⟧⟦D⟧: Continuous turn.
Zoom: Wheel or ⟦W⟧⟦S⟧, zoom lenses only.
AF: Click, ⟦F⟧ or FOCUS. Area AF picks the nearest surface among nine points. ⟦1⟧–⟦9⟧ picks the point.
MF: ⟦Shift⟧ + wheel, ⟦R⟧⟦T⟧ or the slider. With a prime lens the wheel alone works too.
SLR: Line up the two halves of the circle. Rangefinder: Overlap the double image.
Manual exposure: ⟦Q⟧⟦E⟧ aperture, ⟦Z⟧⟦X⟧ shutter speed, ⟦C⟧⟦V⟧ ISO. Mode A: You pick the aperture. Mode S, the time.
Automatic with compensation: ⟦[⟧⟦]⟧ or the wheel over the AUTO button.
⟦Space⟧ shoot · ⟦G⟧ thirds · ⟦Tab⟧ controls over the viewfinder · ⟦I⟧ on-screen help.
⟦Y⟧ lowers the camera to search and brings it back to your eye (classic park).
TLR: You look down into it and the viewfinder swaps left and right. ⟦L⟧ 3× loupe · ⟦K⟧ crank (sandbox, 12 shots).
Arcade: Each level sets the camera, shots, time, minimum score and conditions.
With a controller plugged in, this help shows the controller and its buttons.
raton_rueda: Wheel: Changes the chosen control (zoom at first) · middle click: The next one
raton_arrastrar: Drag: Look (the view goes where you move it)
teclado_objetivo: Zoom ⟦W⟧⟦S⟧ · manual focus ⟦R⟧⟦T⟧ · autofocus ⟦F⟧ · focus point ⟦1⟧–⟦9⟧
teclado_exposicion: Aperture ⟦Q⟧⟦E⟧ · shutter ⟦Z⟧⟦X⟧ · ISO ⟦C⟧⟦V⟧ · compensation ⟦[⟧⟦]⟧ · metering ⟦M⟧ · lock ⟦B⟧
teclado_camara: Pick a control ⟦Tab⟧ and change it ⟦PgUp⟧⟦PgDn⟧ · lower the camera ⟦Y⟧ · thirds ⟦G⟧ · TLR: Loupe ⟦L⟧, crank ⟦K⟧

ayuda_texto_tactil:
Look: Drag a finger across the picture.
Zoom: Pinch with two fingers, or pick Zoom on the strip below and use − and +.
Focus: A tap on the person, or the “AF” button. A long tap focuses and locks focus and exposure.
Shoot: The ● button. Pressing it focuses and releasing it shoots. If you slide your finger off, it doesn't shoot.
Camera settings: Tap one on the strip below and change it with − and +, or slide your finger over it.
Search with your own eyes: “Camera” lowers it and raises it again.
On the left: Thirds, focus and exposure lock, and metering mode.
Big park: The stick walks and dragging your finger looks around. “Run” and “Crouch” stay on.
gfx_subtitulo: All four profiles look the same and only differ in cost. In Custom you set each parameter by hand, even above Ultra.
gfx_aviso: Above Ultra the cost climbs fast: Try one option at a time.
gfx_dof: Depth of field in the viewfinder
gfx_desc_Bajo: Same look at the lowest cost: 50 % resolution (FSR 2), no global illumination or ambient occlusion, and little grass.
gfx_desc_Medio: 70 % resolution, global illumination with 3 cascades, ambient occlusion and 2048 shadows. No volumetric fog.
gfx_desc_Alto: 85 % resolution, full global illumination, volumetric fog, physical penumbra and depth of field in the viewfinder.
gfx_desc_Ultra: Native resolution with 4× MSAA, screen-space reflections and light bounce, full grass and shadows on every streetlight.
gfx_integrada: Integrated graphics: The profiles turn global illumination off (it gives a washed-out image). In Custom you can force it on.
gfx_subtitulo_ligero: On phones and in the browser the game uses a lighter renderer. The profile changes shadows, smoothing and detail: If it runs slowly, go lower.
aviso_rendimiento: The game is running slowly on this computer: Try a lower profile in Options → Graphics.
encargo_busca: Find this person in the park.
encargo_corredor: They're running in sportswear: Mind your shutter speed.
encargo_recuerda: Remember their clothes, hair and accessories.
equipo_modo_a: Aperture priority (A) · you pick the f-stop
equipo_modo_s: Shutter priority (S) · you pick the speed
escenario_clasico_detalle: From the middle of the park
menu_lema: Find the person in your assignment and take their picture. You choose the framing, the focus and the exposure.
menu_clasico_detalle: From the middle of the park, people walk past you
menu_grande_detalle: Explore it on foot and raise your camera whenever you like
menu_pie: Drag to look, wheel to zoom, click to focus, space to shoot.
modo_arcade_texto: Thirty levels with assignments that ask a little more each time: From the automatic compact to the manual TLR, light and panning, each one with something new.
modo_tutorial_texto: Learn to play from scratch, step by step: Looking around, zoom, focus, shooting, reading the result and controlling the exposure. About five minutes.
modo_sandbox_texto: Free photography, with no assignment and no shot limit, with any gear you like. Pick a setting and a light:
modo_academia_texto: Ten photography lessons, each with theory, a demo, practice and an exam: From exposure and composition to cameras, lenses and shooting modes.
modo_opciones_texto: Graphics, gear and game settings; album and badges.
idioma_nota: Se cambia en Opciones · You can change it in Options
modo_historia_texto: A present-day paparazzo and their grandfather, a 1950s press photographer, in a campaign in chapters with the cameras and film of each era. Coming in a future version.
menu_aviso_web_cuerpo: This is the browser version, with simplified graphics. The downloadable version (Windows, Mac and Linux), free on this same page, looks better and handles better.
novedades_graficos: This version changes the default graphics values: We recommend resetting the graphics options with the button below.
novedades_0_6_0_1: The whole game is now in English too: Every text, menu and lesson. Pick the language on first launch and change it any time in Options.
novedades_0_6_0_2: Options, in pairs: Language and theme, gear and exposure steps, look and rumble, album and badges.
novedades_0_6_0_3: Fixes: The photo report no longer repeats what's in the way, and with one shot left it says “1 shot left”.
novedades_0_3_3_1: New wardrobe: Trench coat, tank top, bun, curly hair, beret, backwards cap, backpack, umbrella and glasses.
novedades_0_3_3_2: The camera uses matrix metering unless you choose otherwise, and the on-screen help moves to the I key.
novedades_0_3_3_3: Big park: Steady shadows at golden hour, and the paths by the gazebo no longer flicker.
novedades_0_3_4_1: Third stops: Turn them on in Options to fine-tune aperture, shutter speed and ISO; a full stop is still there with {paso_entero}.
novedades_0_3_4_2: Ten badges, one for each thing the game teaches: Rule of thirds, creamy background, frozen time, street photographer…
novedades_0_3_4_3: Options menu reorganized, and on a controller the D-pad and left stick go through every option.
novedades_0_4_0_1: A 30-level arcade in six blocks: Backlight, silhouette, light trails, everything sharp, what people do… Your progress is kept.
novedades_0_4_0_2: New sound across the whole game: Shutters, dials, footsteps, chatter, animals and an ambience for each light of the day.
novedades_0_4_0_3: The camera exposes better in automatic, and the SLR and the rangefinder reach 1/4000 s.
novedades_0_5_0_1: Far more realistic photos: Real panning and light trails, optical blur on every camera, camera shake, noise and grain.
novedades_0_5_0_2: Hold the turn key toward where someone is going: The camera waits for them, matches their pace and tells you (“Tracking subject”).
novedades_0_5_0_3: The lens matters too: The sun fogs the photo, streetlights turn into stars when you stop down, and at f/22 sharpness drops.
novedades_0_5_1_1: What counts is the face: A tight telephoto close-up is a good frame now, even if the body doesn't fit.
novedades_0_5_1_2: Photos develop faster, especially with graphics above Ultra.
novedades_0_5_2_1: Assignments no longer ask for someone the level's lens can't frame (a faraway child with a 50 mm).
novedades_0_5_3_1: The light meter no longer gets distracted: Matrix metering follows whoever you frame or focus on, even if the point lands just beside them.
novedades_0_5_3_2: Arcade reviewed level by level: No assignment asks for what its camera, light or film can't do.
novedades_0_5_3_3: Panning moves to golden hour, light trails to blue hour and the TLR portrait to sunset: Each photo with its own light.
novedades_0_5_4_1: Manual focus like a real camera: Whoever walks in front shows up split in the viewfinder, and what you had in focus stays put.
novedades_0_5_5_1: Night stars: Stop down to f/11 or more and the streetlights and the bandstand bulbs come out as stars in the photo.
novedades_0_5_5_2: Arcade: Level 20 is now “Starry night”, a handheld night challenge where you choose who to photograph.
novedades_0_5_5_3: Academy: The depth of field lesson ends with a page about the stars of the streetlights.
novedades_0_3_2_1: Android: Full-screen touch interface, with bigger buttons and menus. This version is experimental.
novedades_0_3_2_2: Smoother on phones and browsers, and the characters no longer look dark there.
novedades_0_3_2_3: Clouds only darken the park in arcade levels with manual exposure, and the briefing warns you.
novedades_0_3_1_1: A 60 frames-per-second cap so your computer doesn't work harder than it needs to. Change it in Graphics.
novedades_0_3_1_2: A more natural image: Less contrast, shadows with detail and highlights that don't blow out.
novedades_0_3_1_3: Laptops without a dedicated graphics card start on the Medium profile, with a sensible resolution.
novedades_0_3_0_1: The game is now called PhotoHacks and has a brand-new logo.
novedades_0_3_0_2: Touch interface and first version for Android.
novedades_0_3_0_3: Option to invert the look controls.
novedades_0_2_0_1: The Academy grows to ten lessons, each with its own exam.
novedades_0_2_0_2: The tutorial ends with a stroll through the big park.
novedades_0_2_0_3: The camera settings are handled with the in-hand control.

tutorial_pendiente: Do it and the tutorial will carry on by itself.
tutorial_bienvenida: Welcome to PhotoHacks. You're in the middle of a park with a camera: Your job is to find the person in each assignment and take a good photo of them. Let's go step by step. Press {aceptar} or “Start”.
tutorial_mirar: Look around with {mirar}: To the sides, and up and down too.
tutorial_zoom: Zoom in ({zoom}) past 70 mm, then zoom back out below 40 mm.
tutorial_bajar: With a long lens it's hard to find anyone. Lower the camera to search with your own eyes ({bajar}) and raise it again. A tip: Behind the fence there are only extras. Whoever you're after will always be closer.
tutorial_af: Focus on a person: Aim one of the boxes at them and use autofocus ({af}). You'll hear a beep when it locks.
tutorial_ayuda: The panel on the left is the on-screen help: Your controls, their value and whether you're in charge (MAN) or the camera is (AUTO). Hide it and show it again with {ayuda_pantalla}.
tutorial_disparar: Take a photo of anyone you like: {disparar}. Then you'll see it developed, with its score.
tutorial_seguir: Follow someone who's walking: Hold {girar} toward where they're going. The camera waits for them to reach the focus point and matches their pace: You'll see “Tracking subject”. That's how pans are done.
tutorial_encargo: A real assignment: The description is at the top. Lower the camera ({bajar}) to find that person and raise it for the photo. If there's too much on screen, press {ayuda_pantalla} to clear it.
tutorial_controles: The manual controls work three ways. Pick one with {elegir_tab} and change it with {cambiar_pag}. Click it and use the mouse wheel. Or use its direct shortcut. You'll find the shortcuts with {ayuda}.
tutorial_diafragma: Aperture priority (A): You're in charge of the aperture. Change it twice: Pick it on the strip below and turn the wheel, or use its shortcut, {diafragma_y}.
tutorial_tercios: A tip: In Options you can switch “Exposure steps” to thirds for finer control. The same controls then move a third of a stop; with {paso_entero}, a full stop.
tutorial_abruma: Just a reminder: If you see too much information, you can toggle the help with {ayuda_pantalla}. The strip below stays: Click whatever you want to change, then the wheel. It only shows what you can change at that moment.
tutorial_mf: Manual focus: Pick Focus on the strip and turn the wheel, or use its shortcut ({enfoque_mf_zoom}), until the two halves of the center circle line up on someone.
tutorial_controles_mando: The manual controls are on the strip below. Pick one with {elegir_control} and change it with {cambiar_control}. Zoom and manual focus are also on the right stick. You can check every button with {ayuda}.
tutorial_diafragma_mando: Aperture priority (A): You're in charge of the aperture. Change it twice: Pick it on the strip below with {elegir_control} and change it with {cambiar_control}.
tutorial_abruma_mando: Just a reminder: If you see too much information, you can toggle the on-screen help with {ayuda_pantalla}. The strip below stays, and it only shows the controls you can change at that moment.
tutorial_mf_mando: Manual focus: Turn the ring with {enfoque_mf_zoom} until the two halves of the center circle line up on someone.
tutorial_paseo: This is the big park, and here you walk. With the camera lowered, walk with {andar} and look with {mirar_paseo}. Walk a few meters.
tutorial_sacar: To take photos you have to raise the camera: {sacar}. You can't walk with it at your eye: You walk and search with the camera lowered, and raise it only to shoot. Raise it.
tutorial_foto_paseo: Take a photo of anyone you like ({disparar}), then lower the camera ({sacar}) so you can keep walking.
tutorial_resultado_paseo: Done. Now lower the camera to keep walking.
tutorial_bienvenida_tactil: Welcome to PhotoHacks. You're in the middle of a park with a camera: Your job is to find the person in each assignment and take a good photo of them. Let's go step by step. Tap “Start”.
tutorial_mirar_tactil: Look around by dragging a finger across the picture: To the sides, and up and down too.
tutorial_zoom_tactil: Zoom in by pinching with two fingers (or with Zoom on the strip below and +) past 70 mm, then zoom back out below 40 mm.
tutorial_encargo_tactil: A real assignment: The description is at the top. Lower the camera with “Camera” to find that person and raise it for the photo. They need to be whole, in focus and with nobody blocking them.
tutorial_controles_tactil: The manual controls are on the strip below. Tap the one you want to change and use the − and + buttons. Only the ones you can change at that moment appear. The other gestures are in “Help”.
tutorial_diafragma_tactil: Aperture priority (A): You're in charge of the aperture. Tap it on the strip below and change it twice with − and +.
tutorial_mf_tactil: Manual focus: Tap Focus on the strip and use − and + (hold them to go faster) until the two halves of the center circle line up on someone.
tutorial_paseo_tactil: This is the big park, and here you walk. With the camera lowered, walk with the stick on the left and look by dragging a finger across the screen. Walk a few meters.
tutorial_sacar_tactil: To take photos you have to raise the camera with “Camera”. You can't walk with it at your eye: You walk and search with the camera lowered, and raise it only to shoot. Raise it.
tutorial_foto_paseo_tactil: Take a photo of anyone you like with ●, then lower the camera with “Camera” so you can keep walking.
tutorial_fin_tactil: You know the basics now: Looking, focusing, shooting, changing the controls and moving around. Choose how to carry on. You can go over the gestures any time in “Help”.
tutorial_fin: You know the basics now: Looking, focusing, shooting, changing the controls and moving around. Choose how to carry on. You can go over the controls any time with {ayuda}.
tutorial_ir_arcade_texto: The way forward: 30 short levels, each with its own assignment and a new control.
tutorial_ir_academia_texto: Ten lessons to understand the photography behind it: Light, focus, composition, cameras and lenses.
tutorial_repetir_texto: Start over from the first step.
tutorial_menu_texto: Every mode, the gear and the options.
tutorial_resultado_disparar: This is the developed photo: The score comes from focus, exposure, motion, what's blocked and the framing. Press Continue to go on.
tutorial_resultado_bien: Assignment done with %d points! Press Continue to go on.
tutorial_resultado_otra: Not yet: Check the report on the right and try again.

mirar_y_encontrar_arrastra_horizontalmen:
LOOK AND FIND
Drag sideways or use A/D and the arrows. W/S or wheel: Zoom.
Click on the scene: Picks the nearest AF point and focuses.
F: Focus again · 1–9: AF point · G: Thirds grid.

ADJUST AND SHOOT
Q/E: Aperture · Z/X: Shutter speed · C/V: ISO · R/T: Focus distance.
You can also click or drag the values on the top bar. Right-click: Decrease.
Space: Shoot · Enter: Continue · Esc: Close help · ?: Open help.

ON A TOUCH SCREEN
One finger: Pan with inertia · Pinch: Zoom · Two fingers up and down: Manual focus.
A tap: AF point and focus · Drag a setting to change it.

READ THE LIGHT
Needle at 0: Correct exposure. Positive ΔEV: Dark photo. Negative: Too bright.
At long focal lengths, use shorter times. For more sharpness, focus and stop down.
The camera stays at 1.60 m: At 24 mm the adults on the 4 m lane fit.
el_objetivo_esta_fuera_del_encuadre_su_p: Your subject is out of frame: Their face must be inside the picture.

el_sujeto_esta_dentro_de_la_nitidez_acep: The subject is within acceptable sharpness.
abre_diafragma_sube_iso_o_alarga_el_tiem: Open the aperture, raise the ISO or use a longer time.
cierra_diafragma_baja_iso_o_acorta_el_ti: Stop down, lower the ISO or use a shorter time.
usa_1_d_s_o_mas_rapido_para_congelar_est: Use 1/%d s or faster to freeze this motion.
velocidad_suficiente_para_pulso_y_sujeto: Fast enough for your hands and the subject.
